problems.statement: Let f(n) count the k ≤ n with k·σ(k) = n, where σ is the sum-of-divisors function. Show: (i) for some h(n) = o(1/log log n), f(n) ≤ n^{h(n)} for all large n; (ii) for some constant C, f(n) = O((log n)^C).

Let σ be the sum-of-divisors function, and let S(x) count ordered pairs of positive integers (a, b) with a + b ≤ x and σ(a) + σ(b) = σ(a + b). Does there exist a constant c > 0 such that S(x) is asymptotic to c·x as x → ∞?
There are only finitely many pairs of natural numbers (n, k) with k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 2k such that the least prime factor of the binomial coefficient C(n, k) exceeds max(⌊n/k⌋, k).

Let A, B be infinite sets of natural numbers whose n-th smallest elements a_n, b_n satisfy a_n/b_n → 1. If A + B contains all sufficiently large integers, must the number of representations n = a + b (a ∈ A, b ∈ B) be unbounded?

Does there exist a constant c > 0 such that, for all sufficiently large n, every complex polynomial P of degree n with every coefficient (from degree 0 to n) equal to −1 or 1 satisfies max over |z| = 1 of |P(z)| > (1 + c)·√n?

Let p_n denote the n-th prime. Is it true that there is a continuous function f: [0, ∞) → ℝ such that, for every c ≥ 0, the set of natural numbers n with (p_{n+1} − p_n)/log n < c has natural density f(c)?

Is it true that for every strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers n_0 < n_1 < n_2 < ⋯ with limsup_{k→∞} n_k/(k+1) = ∞, the real number ∑_{k≥0} 1/2^{n_k} is transcendental (over the rationals)?

Is the real number Σ_{n=0}^∞ q_n / 2^n irrational, where q_n is the n-th prime counting from zero (q_0 = 2, q_1 = 3, q_2 = 5, …)? Equivalently, is Σ_{n≥1} p_n / 2^n irrational, where p_n is the n-th prime with p_1 = 2?

Let A ⊆ ℕ satisfy |A ∩ (x, 2x]| → ∞ as x → ∞, and suppose Σ_{n∈A} ‖θn‖ diverges for every θ ∈ (0,1), where ‖·‖ is the distance to the nearest integer. Then every sufficiently large integer is a sum of distinct elements of A.

For N ≥ 1, let f(N) be the largest t such that there are distinct subsets A_1, …, A_t of {1, …, N} with every A_i ∩ A_j (i ≠ j) a non-empty arithmetic progression. Find an explicit g(N) with f(N) ~ g(N) as N → ∞.

Let A be a set of natural numbers such that all but finitely many natural numbers are of the form a + b with a, b ∈ A. Then the number of representations of n as a + b (a, b ∈ A) is unbounded as n → ∞.

Is it true that for all sufficiently large k there are k pairwise disjoint intervals [a_i, b_i] of natural numbers, each with a_i < b_i, such that the sum over all i of Σ_{n=a_i}^{b_i} 1/n equals 1? (Here 1/0 counts as 0.)
For n ≥ 1, let L_n = lcm(1, …, n), and define a_n by 1 + 1/2 + … + 1/n = a_n / L_n. Are there infinitely many n for which gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1?
For k ≥ 3, let f_k(x) be the number of integers at most x that are sums of three kth powers. Is it true that for every k ≥ 3 some c > 0 has f_k(x) ≥ c·x^(3/k) for all sufficiently large x?

Over all Sidon sets A ⊆ ℕ (sets where the sums a + b with a ≤ b are all distinct), what is the supremum of

limsup as N → ∞ of |A ∩ {1,…,N}| / N^{1/2}?

Let A = {1, 2, 4, 8, 13, ...} be the greedy Sidon sequence: start with 1, then repeatedly add the smallest integer keeping a+b=c+d free of non-trivial solutions. Is it true that for every ε>0 there is c>0 with |A ∩ {1,…,N}| ≥ c·N^{1/2−ε} for all large N?

Is it true that for every integer sequence a_0, a_1, … in which, for all sufficiently large n, a_{n+1} is the least integer exceeding a_n not of the form a_i + a_j (i, j ≤ n), the differences a_{m+1} − a_m are eventually periodic?

Find all pairs of natural numbers m < n such that some nondecreasing natural-number sequence stays complete after zeroing the terms at any m indices, but not after zeroing the terms at any n indices. Complete: every sufficiently large integer is a sum of distinct values of the sequence.
Does there exist a positive integer n such that n is 2-full (every prime dividing n divides it at least squared) and n+1 is 3-full (every prime dividing n+1 divides it at least cubed)?
Is there an integer k ≥ 2 such that, for infinitely many n with k ≤ n − 2, the binomial coefficient C(n, k) is a product of consecutive primes p_a·p_{a+1}⋯p_{b−1}, where p_i is the i-th prime?

Does there exist a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers 1 ≤ d_0 < d_1 < d_2 < ..., whose set of values has natural density 1, such that the block products d_u · d_{u+1} · ... · d_v (for u ≤ v) are distinct for distinct pairs (u, v)?
Let S be the smallest set of integers containing 2 and 3 such that ab − 1 ∈ S whenever a and b are distinct elements of S. Does S have positive density?

For a transcendental entire function f(z) = Σ a_n z^n, let M(r) = max over |z| = r of |f(z)| and ratio(r) = max_n |a_n| r^n / M(r). What is the supremum, over all such f, of liminf as r → ∞ of ratio(r)?

Is there a constant c > 0 such that every Rademacher multiplicative function f, on any probability space, almost surely satisfies limsup as N → ∞ of (Σ_{m≤N} f(m)) / sqrt(N log log N) = c, with the same c for all such f?

For r ≥ 3, let f_r(N) be the largest size of a subset of {1,…,N} with no r elements whose pairwise gcds are all equal. Show that for every r ≥ 3 some c > 0 has f_r(N) ≤ N^(c / log log N) for all sufficiently large N.

Let m be an infinite set and κ the successor cardinal of 2^ℵ0. Can the countable subsets of m be coloured with κ colours so that, for every X ⊆ m with |X| = κ, every colour is attained by some countable subset of X?

Let r ≥ 3. For every colouring of the edges of the complete graph on r^2 + 1 vertices with r colours, there exist a set S of r + 1 vertices and a colour k such that no edge between two distinct vertices of S has colour k.

Let ε_n be the supremum of ε such that residues a_p can be chosen for the primes n^ε < p ≤ n with every integer in [1,n] congruent to a_p mod p for some such p. Find f(n) with f = O(ε_n) and ε_n = O(f). Does ε_n → 0?
Is it true that for all sufficiently large n, one can choose a residue a_p for each prime p ≤ n such that every integer m with 1 ≤ m ≤ n satisfies m ≡ a_p (mod p) for at least two primes p ≤ n?
Is it true that, as n → ∞ over natural numbers, the sum of 1/p over all primes p ≤ n for which the remainder n mod p is greater than p/2 is asymptotic to (log log n)/2, i.e. their ratio tends to 1?

Does there exist a graph G with ℵ_1 vertices and chromatic number ℵ_1 such that, for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large n, every subgraph of G on n vertices contains more than n^(1−ε) of its vertices forming an independent set in G?

(1) Is there k > 2 such that the k-subsets of {1,…,2k} can be (k+1)-coloured so that every (k+1)-subset contains k-subsets of all colours? (2) For every k ≥ 3, is the chromatic number of the Johnson graph J(2k,k) (k-subsets, adjacent when sharing k−1 elements) at least k+2?

Are there infinitely many natural numbers n such that, in the prime factorisation of n(n+1), distinct primes always appear with distinct exponents? That is, no two different prime factors of n(n+1) have the same exponent.

(i) Is there a graph with ℵ_2 vertices and chromatic number ℵ_2 whose ℵ_1-vertex induced subgraphs all have chromatic number ≤ ℵ_0? (ii) For every ordinal α, is there a graph with ℵ_{α+1} vertices and chromatic number ℵ_1 whose ℵ_α-vertex induced subgraphs all have chromatic number ≤ ℵ_0?

Is it true that for all natural numbers k1 ≥ k2 ≥ 3, there are only finitely many pairs of natural numbers (n1, n2) with n2 ≥ n1 + k1 such that (n1+1)(n1+2)…(n1+k1) and (n2+1)(n2+2)…(n2+k2) have exactly the same set of prime factors?
Let f(n) be the maximum number of pairs at distance exactly 1 among n points in the plane that form the vertices of a convex polygon. Is f(n) = O(n) as n → ∞?

Three problems:

1. Show that the sequence (3/2)^n, n = 0, 1, 2, …, is equidistributed modulo 1.
2. Show that for every real x transcendental over the rationals, the sequence x·(3/2)^n is equidistributed modulo 1.
3. Find an explicit accumulation point of the sequence of fractional parts of (3/2)^n.

Do there exist constants C, c > 0 such that, for every group G (not necessarily abelian), every K ≥ 1 and every finite K-approximate subgroup A of G, there is a subset S ⊆ A with |S| ≥ C·K^(−c)·|A| and S^8 ⊆ A^4 (product sets)?
Is it true that every open set A ⊆ [0,1] with Lebesgue measure greater than 1/3 contains x, y, z (not necessarily distinct) with xy = z?

Let H(r) be the radius-r Hamming ball in F_2^n, and f(r) the liminf over n of the minimum of |V|·|H(r)|/2^n over subspaces V with V + H(r) = F_2^n. Determine whether (1) f(r) → ∞ as r → ∞; (2) f(r) = 1 for all r; (3) f(2) = 1.

For ε > 0, let N(ε) be the fewest rotations about the origin of {(x, y) ∈ R^2 : dist(x, Z) ≤ ε} covering R^2. Find an explicit B(ε) such that, for some C > 0 and all small enough ε > 0, N(ε) ≤ B(ε) < exp(exp(exp(ε^(-C)))).

Let F(α,n) be the largest d such that A + A contains a d-dimensional coset whenever A ⊆ F_2^n has density ≥ α. Determine F. Also: does every C > 0 admit c with F(α,n) ≥ n − c for large n and α ∈ (1/2 − C/√n, 1]?

Let γ be the standard Gaussian product measure on real sequences ℕ → ℝ. Is it true that every compact balanced set K (λK ⊆ K whenever |λ| ≤ 1) with γ(K) ≥ 0.99 satisfies: 10K contains a compact convex set C with γ(C) ≥ 0.01?

For n points in the unit disc, let α(n) be the largest possible value of the smallest area of a triangle formed by three of the points. Is there a function o(n) → 0 such that α(n) ≤ C·n^(−2+o(n)) for some constant C and all sufficiently large n?

Does every measurable set A ⊂ ℝ of positive Lebesgue measure contain an affine copy of {1, 1/2, 1/4, ...}? That is, must there exist real numbers a ≠ 0 and b such that a·(1/2^n) + b ∈ A for every natural number n ≥ 0?

There are infinitely many natural numbers m such that m^2 + π(m) is prime, where π(m) is the number of primes ≤ m. (Equivalently, OEIS sequence A228828, listing these m, takes infinitely many values.)

For every n ≥ 7, every rank-2 vector bundle on complex projective n-space P^n over ℂ splits as a direct sum of two line bundles. Equivalently, no indecomposable rank-2 vector bundles exist on P^n for n ≥ 7.

For every n and every Boolean function f: {0,1}^n → {0,1}, bs(f) ≤ s(f)^2. Here s(f) is the maximum over inputs x of the number of bits whose flip changes f(x); bs(f) is the maximum number of disjoint bit-blocks whose flips each change f(x).

problems.display_name: Paper: Voronovskaja-type Formula for the Bezier Variant of the Bernstein Operators
problems.statement: Let B_{n,α} f(x) = Σ_{k=0}^n f(k/n)[J_{n,k}(x)^α − J_{n,k+1}(x)^α] with J_{n,k}(x) = Σ_{j≥k} C(n,j) x^j (1−x)^{n−j} and J_{n,n+1} = 0. For α > 0, α ≠ 1, f twice continuously differentiable on [0,1], and x ∈ [0,1], determine lim_{n→∞} √n (B_{n,α} f(x) − f(x)).

problems.display_name: Wikipedia: Euler's sum of powers conjecture
problems.statement: For integers n > 1 and k ≥ 6, if positive integers a_1, …, a_n and a natural number b satisfy a_1^k + a_2^k + … + a_n^k = b^k, then n ≥ k.
Let p_n be the n-th prime, with p_1 = 2. Then the sequence p_n^(1/n) is strictly decreasing: for every n ≥ 1, p_(n+1)^(1/(n+1)) < p_n^(1/n).

problems.display_name: Wikipedia: Convergence of the Flint Hills and Cookson Hills series
problems.statement:
Determine whether each of the following series converges:

1. The Flint Hills series: the sum over n ≥ 1 of 1/(n^3 sin^2 n).
2. The Cookson Hills series: the sum over n ≥ 1 of 1/(n^3 cos^2 n).

Here n is in radians.

Let n, k ≥ 1 and suppose n, n+1, …, n+k−1 are all composite.

1. There exist distinct primes p_0, …, p_{k−1} such that p_i divides n+i for each i from 0 to k−1.
2. (Weaker) There exist k distinct primes, each dividing at least one of n, …, n+k−1.
(a) Some C > 0 has |y^2 − x^3| > C·|x|^(1/2) for all integers x, y with y^2 ≠ x^3. (b) For every ε > 0, some C > 0 has |y^2 − x^3| > C·|x|^(1/2 − ε) for all integers x, y with y^2 ≠ x^3.
Let R be a ring, and let I and J be left ideals of R that are nil (every element is nilpotent). Then I + J is also nil: every element of I + J is nilpotent.
π is normal in base 10: in its decimal expansion, every finite string of k digits occurs with limiting frequency 10^(-k).
Are there infinitely many natural numbers n such that n^2 + 1 is prime? Equivalently, are there infinitely many primes p for which p − 1 is a perfect square?
Let τ(n) be the Ramanujan tau function, defined by q ∏_{k≥1} (1 − q^k)^24 = Σ_{n≥1} τ(n) q^n. Prove that τ(n) ≠ 0 for every positive integer n.
There are infinitely many regular primes. A prime p is regular if p does not divide the class number of the p-th cyclotomic field Q(ζ_p).

Let fs be a finite set of nonconstant irreducible integer polynomials with positive leading coefficients. Suppose that for every prime p there is a natural number n with p dividing no f(n), f in fs. Then infinitely many natural numbers n make |f(n)| prime for every f in fs.

templates.forecast:
Today's date is {run_date}.

Below are {n_items} problems in mathematics, taken from two public trackers: the Erdős Problems database (github.com/teorth/erdosproblems) and Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository. Each problem was listed as open on {t0}. Some have since been resolved and some have not; you do not know what has happened to them since {t0}.

A problem counts as solved on the date a tracker records it as proved, disproved, solved or shown independent. Partial results and special cases do not count.

For each problem, give three dates in the format YYYY-MM:
- "best": your best guess of when it is (or was) solved;
- "q10": a date by which you think there is a 10% chance it is solved;
- "q90": a date by which you think there is a 90% chance it is solved.
Use "after-2100" for any date later than 2100. Dates may lie between {t0_month} and today if you think the problem may already have been solved. No date may be earlier than {t0_month}. Each problem must satisfy q10 <= best <= q90.

Problems:
{items}

Reply with a JSON array only, one object per problem, in any order:
[{{"id": "<problem id>", "best": "YYYY-MM", "q10": "YYYY-MM", "q90": "YYYY-MM"}}, ...]
templates.reveal_solved:
Here is what happened between {t0} and {snapshot_date}, according to the trackers.

{n_solved} of the {n_items} problems above were solved in that period. This share is not representative. {n_guaranteed} of the {n_items} problems were deliberately chosen from problems that were solved in this period; the other {n_random} were drawn at random from all {n_eligible} eligible problems that were open on {t0}, and {n_random_solved} of those {n_random} were solved. Across all {n_eligible} eligible problems, {n_pool_solved} ({pool_pct}%) were solved by {snapshot_date}.

The solved problems, with your earlier forecast for each:

{solved_items}

The other {n_open} problems were still open on {snapshot_date}. Taking this information into account, give revised forecasts for these {n_open} problems, in the same format as before:

{open_items}

Use "after-2100" for any date later than 2100. No date may be earlier than {s_month}. Each problem must satisfy q10 <= best <= q90.

Reply with a JSON array only, one object per problem, in any order:
[{{"id": "<problem id>", "best": "YYYY-MM", "q10": "YYYY-MM", "q90": "YYYY-MM"}}, ...]
